summary:
Portfolio net worth hovers around M$545 with spendable balance pinned at M$1 due to extended resolution latency, as closed markets from the Aug 11-14 cluster remain locked before mana unlocks. Active exposure consists of 10 positions: high-conviction tech and finance shorts, a personal relationship market closing in late August, and structural timeline holdings. The primary negative development was the complete failure of the high-conviction "Will something happen in AI the week of Aug 21, 2026?" (dlL65QERsl) position, which initially tricked us with a correction from 82% down to 69% YES before sharply reversing to hit 100% YES, resulting in a M$37 loss. All other open positions are in profit and pass the re-open test. Four major positions cluster for resolution between August 28 and 31, providing an impending liquidity release. Social gifts include a tracked M$50 return obligation to cA1JupYR5AR8btHUs2xvkui7jA93 and a recent M$10 gift from y5RkCJ45bRTdfdoln6wRM4qLHli1. 

Concrete mistakes to avoid include letting spendable mana drop near operational floors without accounting for resolution latency (specifically the two-phase gap between market closure and mana unfreezing); falling into the stale execution trap by deploying capital into pre-computed watchlists after edges compress; treating temporary price corrections in timeline markets as definitive validation without real-world falsification; holding positions after their core thesis is contradicted; dabbling in vague sentiment markets or marginal tactical bets; and succumbing to activity bias—making suboptimal trades or misinterpreting false price signals just to feel productive during periods of forced inactivity.

Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic timeline claims, symbolic developer hype, and speculative community propositions, while personal relationship markets and ambiguous sentiment bets require strict discipline. The core lesson is that downward price drift in hype markets can be a deceptive false signal rather than a structural correction, requiring tighter invalidation criteria and primary reliance on real-world falsification rather than secondary price action. 

Standing priorities are maintaining operational discipline during forced inactivity while awaiting the end-of-August liquidity wave, avoiding activity bias, honoring tracked social obligations when liquidity permits, and maintaining a clean, high-signal decision-making environment without redundant notes.
